title: TSR: AFE isoSPI Communication Integrity

standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the record was written from the clause's concept ('hardware safety requirements'). Where the same rationale also says that no clause text was reproduced or consulted, that is a RIGHTS statement about wording, not a statement about influence: the record took the concept's shape and not its words, which is why the clause is its derivation basis. It is not a conformance claim - no clause was audited against this record and no assessment was performed.

The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('hardware requirements and architecture'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: foxBMS 2 publishes no hardware safety requirements. The isoSPI interface is documented in an Altium design file in a separate repository, and this record was written by this corpus from the CAN frames the pinned firmware exchanges.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees a hardware requirement at ASIL_D with a BER < 10^-9 figure and a mapping to ISO 26262 Part 5 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the interface integrity is a characterised, verified hardware property. No bit-error measurement exists in this corpus, the 5 ms detection figure is unsourced, and the clause is the basis of the requirement's shape rather than something the interface was measured against.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/driver/can/cbs/tx-cyclic/can_cbs_tx_f_cell-voltages.c:238-305 (CANTX_CellVoltages) and src/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c:155-182 (CANRX_CellVoltages) for the cyclic frames that carry the measured cell voltages across the interface; and FB2-SRC-HW-000003 - an Altium .SchDoc in the separate foxBMS2_hw repository, absent here, content hash 'unresolved'.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned firmware exchanges the measured cell voltages over the interface this requirement is about, so integrity and failure detection on that path are real subjects. It supports NOTHING about the BER or the 5 ms: no measurement of either exists in this repository, and a code path that frames a message is not a measurement of its error rate.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Added asil_allocation_scope, and moved the origin field from source_observed to derived. An independent audit flagged this record as asserting an unqualified ASIL on an as_is profile record, which presents a classification belonging to the hypothetical reference project as though it were a determination about the real foxBMS product. The ASIL value itself is untouched and remains ASIL_D, because it is legitimate inside the fictional project; what is different now is that the value can no longer be read without the reconstruction stated alongside it. The origin move is required by master prompt section 5: this record carries a back-inferred classification alongside source-derived content, so it may not be labelled wholly observed. It was previously source_observed.

revision_history.author: corpus_governance
revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect this corrects is legibility, not content: this record was already honest in `origin: derived` and in revision prose, but a reader skimming `artifact_type` and `standards_mappings` would take requirement for something the foxBMS 2 project published and its ISO 26262 mapping for a claim of satisfaction. Neither is true, and the correction now says so in declarative fields on the record itself. derivation_basis names the file:line or the corpus record the derivation actually rests on, and states what it does not support, so a grader can check the derivation instead of taking it on trust. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: The isoSPI interface shall provide communication with BER < 10^-9 and detect communication failures within 5 ms.
rationale: Communication failures must be detected within FTTI budget for AFE data

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from communication loss to SW notification

provenance_note: Provenance re-checked 2026-10-01 after the source-registry repair. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000021 and -000023 previously named CAN_TX_CellVoltages and CAN_RX_AFE_CellVoltages, neither of which exists; they now name CANTX_CellVoltages (can_cbs_tx_f_cell-voltages.c:238-305) and CANRX_CellVoltages (can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c:155-182). Those are CAN transport callbacks, not the isoSPI link, and neither states a bit error rate. Anchor FB2-SRC-HW-000003 points at an LTC6820 schematic absent from foxbms-2. The BER < 1e-9 and 5 ms figures are datasheet claims. Reconstructed from those claims, so labelled derived, not source_observed.

asil_allocation_scope.classification_belongs_to: the hypothetical reference project declared by the synthetic_reference profile of this corpus
asil_allocation_scope.statement: The asil value in this record's safety_allocation is a RECONSTRUCTED value, not an observation and not a determination. It was produced by reading back the safety-goal classification of the hypothetical reference project this corpus also declares in its synthetic_reference profile, and by attributing that classification to this record because this corpus's own requirement set was written downstream of it. The real foxBMS 2 product has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment. No HARA has been performed for it, none is claimed here, and nothing in this record may be read as one, as a partial one, or as a substitute for one.
asil_allocation_scope.why_the_value_is_still_here: The ASIL is retained rather than deleted because it is legitimate inside the fictional project: the reference project needs an allocated class at this element for its own argument to be internally consistent, and removing the number would leave the reference project's allocation silently unallocated. What was illegitimate was its presentation here, as an unqualified field on an as_is record that a reader could take as a statement about the product. That presentation is what this field removes.
what_this_field_asserts: That the recorded asil value equals the classification the reference project's safety concept and goal chain assigns to this element, as those records state it.
That the classification originates in the reference project and nowhere else.
That no classification has been performed for the real product by this corpus or by anyone on its behalf.
what_this_field_does_not_assert: It does not assert an ASIL for the real foxBMS 2 product. The real product's safety integrity level is undetermined, not ASIL_D; undetermined is the honest answer and this corpus has no standing to change it.
It does not assert that a hazard analysis and risk assessment exists for the real product in any form, complete or partial.

It does not assert that any design, in either profile, meets this ASIL. An allocation creates an obligation downstream; it is not evidence the obligation is discharged, and no execution record in this corpus discharges it for this element.
It does not assert ISO 26262 conformity, certification, or qualification of any product, supplier, tool or process.
It does not assert an Automotive SPICE capability level for any organisation.

It does not assert that the exposure or severity inputs behind the reference project's classification are evidenced. They are authored: the reference project's safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 already records that its exposure rating is an unevidenced authored input and that a single exposure step would move the whole classification one class lower.
asil_allocation_scope.reading_rule: Any view, report or export that renders this record's asil value must render this field with it. An asil value shown without this field is a defect in that view, not a permissible abbreviation.
asil_allocation_scope.origin_field_relationship: Because this record now carries a back-inferred classification alongside its source-derived content, origin is 'derived' rather than 'source_observed': master prompt section 5 requires that an artefact containing both observed and modelled content must not be labelled wholly observed. Where this record's origin was 'source_observed' it has been changed to 'derived' for that reason and for no other; no statement, acceptance criterion, threshold, assumption, safety goal reference or mitigation text was altered in the same edit.
